questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: At what vertebral level is the lower border of the pharynx?
questions.explanation: The lower border of the pharynx is at the level of C6 (the source explanation also notes C6/C7). The pharynx extends from the cranial base to the lower border of the cricoid cartilage and is divided into the nasopharynx, oropharynx, and laryngopharynx.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: An ENT resident is performing endoscopy of the nasopharynx in a patient with suspected nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Which of the following structures is not expected to be seen there?
questions.explanation: The piriform fossa is a feature of the laryngopharynx, not the nasopharynx. Structures seen in the nasopharynx include the opening of the eustachian tube, torus tubarius, the fossa of Rosenmuller behind the torus, the pharyngeal tonsil, and Passavant’s ridge. The fossa of Rosenmuller is an important site for nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following structures form Passavant’s ridge?
questions.explanation: Passavant’s ridge is formed by the palatopharyngeus and superior constrictor. Some fibers of palatopharyngeus form an internal sphincter superior to the superior constrictor; contraction produces a ridge on the posterior wall of the nasopharynx.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 9-year-old girl with pharyngitis develops ear pain and a blocked sensation. Where does the involved structure open in the nasopharynx?

options.text: Behind posterior end of inferior turbinate

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind posterior end of inferior turbinate
questions.explanation: The symptoms suggest spread to the middle ear through the eustachian tube. Its nasopharyngeal opening lies approximately behind the posterior end of the inferior turbinate on the lateral wall of the nasopharynx. The tube connects the nasopharynx to the middle ear, is normally collapsed, and opens during yawning and swallowing.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 16-year-old presents with sore throat and fever, and the image shows purulent tonsils. Which of the following structures will not be seen in the oropharynx?
questions.explanation: The image is consistent with acute tonsillitis. Passavant’s ridge lies on the posterior wall of the nasopharynx and is not an oropharyngeal structure. The oropharynx extends from below the soft palate to the upper border of the epiglottis and includes the palatoglossal folds, palatopharyngeal folds, palatine tonsils between them, lingual tonsils, and valleculae.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: During indirect laryngoscopy to visualize the hypopharynx, which of the following structures is not seen?
questions.explanation: Valleculae belong to the oropharynx and are not part of the hypopharynx. The hypopharynx or laryngopharynx extends from the superior border of the epiglottis to the lower border of the cricoid cartilage. Its landmarks include the laryngeal inlet, posterior pharyngeal wall, postcricoid region, and piriform fossae. The piriform fossa lies between the aryepiglottic fold medially and the thyroid cartilage/thyrohyoid membrane laterally; internal laryngeal branches run beneath its mucosa.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Where is the sinus of Morgagni?
questions.explanation: The sinus of Morgagni is the gap between the skull base and the upper border of the superior constrictor. It transmits the palatine branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery, ascending palatine artery, levator veli palatini, and the eustachian tube. The source also notes Trotter’s triad in nasopharyngeal carcinoma: conductive hearing loss, ipsilateral palatal immobility, and neuralgic pain.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 46-year-old with dysphagia and regurgitation has a pulsion diverticulum on barium swallow. Weakness of which muscle predisposes to this condition?
questions.explanation: The finding is a Zenker diverticulum, which protrudes through Killian’s dehiscence in the inferior constrictor. The upper thyropharyngeus has oblique fibers and the lower cricopharyngeus has transverse fibers; the weak area between them is Killian’s dehiscence. The source also describes Laimer’s triangle between the cricopharyngeus and longitudinal muscle of the esophagus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following muscles is not supplied by the pharyngeal plexus?
questions.explanation: Stylopharyngeus is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve and is the exception. The pharyngeal plexus is formed by pharyngeal branches of the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves with sympathetic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion. It supplies the soft-palate muscles except tensor veli palatini, and the pharyngeal muscles except stylopharyngeus.
